这应该由船只要求比较紧急的情况下可以决定超越码头要求的船只管理团队来判断
CD0283 — Hot work, Management of hot wor.answer: 不行 – 尽管 SMS 允许，但码头法规优先

CD0283 — Hot work, Management of hot wor.question: On a tanker, hot work repairs are to be carried out on the main deck at a height of 760mm above the tank top. The ship is not inerted. Within what specified distance of the repair must other tanks be cleaned and gas freed or filled with water?
在一艘油轮上，要在罐体之上 760 毫米处的甲板上进行高温作业维修。船只未惰性处理。必须对距离维修多大规定距离内的其他油罐进行清洁和气体排空或充水？

The transfer to another tank on board and isolation of slops is a requirement in many hot work situations. Is there an alternative to this requirement that might apply in certain circumstances? If so, what is it?
options: Yes – the slops can be removed from the vessel
No – this is an absolute requirement and there is no alternative
Yes – the tank containing the slops can be inerted. They do not have to be moved if this is done
Yes – the tank containing the slops can be continuously ventilated during the hot work procedure. They do not have to be moved if this is done
CD0283 — Hot work, Management of hot wor.answer: Yes – the slops can be removed from the vessel

CD0283 — Hot work, Management of hot wor.question: 在很多高温作业情况下均要求转移到船上的另一个油罐和隔离污水。对于此要求是否具有适用于某些情况的其他替代要求？ 如果有，是什么？
options: 有 - 污水可以处理到船舶之外。
没有 - 这是绝对要求，没有备用方式。
有 - 污水罐可以进行惰性处理。如果进行了惰性处理则无需移走。
有 - 污水罐可以在高温作业期间持续通风。如果进行了惰性处理则无需移走。
CD0283 — Hot work, Management of hot wor.answer: 有 - 污水可以处理到船舶之外。

CD0283 — Hot work, Management of hot wor.question: A hot work repair is to take place on a bracket in a fuel tank. The tank has been cleaned and gas freed. How should the heating coils in the tank be treated before the hot work begins?
options: They should be flushed or blown through with steam and then tested to ensure they are clear of hydrocarbons
They should be continuously blown through with fresh air whilst the hot work repair is taking place
They should be disconnected and removed from the tank
They should be continuously blown through with inert gas whilst the hot work is taking place
CD0283 — Hot work, Management of hot wor.answer: They should be flushed or blown through with steam and then tested to ensure they are clear of hydrocarbons

CD0283 — Hot work, Management of hot wor.question: 要对燃油罐内的支架进行高温作业维修。罐体已经清洁且排空了气体。高温作业开始之前应该如何处理罐体内的加热线圈？
options: 应该冲刷或使用蒸汽吹扫，然后进行测试，确保没有碳氢化合物。
进行高温作业维修时应该使用新鲜空气持续吹扫。
应该将其断开并从罐体取下。
进行高温作业时应该使用惰性气体持续吹扫。
CD0283 — Hot work, Management of hot wor.answer: 应该冲刷或使用蒸汽吹扫，然后进行测试，确保没有碳氢化合物。

CD0283 — Hot work, Management of hot wor.question: Who signs off a hot work permit, indicating whether or not the work has been completed?
options: The authorised person
The competent person
The safety officer
The hot work officer
CD0283 — Hot work, Management of hot wor.answer: The authorised person

CD0283 — Hot work, Management of hot wor.question: 谁应该签署高温作业许可证，表明作业是否已完成？
options: 授权人员
有资格人员
安全官
高温作业官员
CD0283 — Hot work, Management of hot wor.answer: 授权人员

CD0283 — Hot work, Management of hot wor.question: A welder is working in a confined and restricted area and in close contact with the ship’s structure. How can the welder be additionally protected against the risk of electric shock through touching the hull or frames?
options: By providing dry insulating mats or boards
By wearing safety boots
By wearing a cotton coverall
By washing down the area with freshwater before welding commences
CD0283 — Hot work, Management of hot wor.answer: By providing dry insulating mats or boards

CD0283 — Hot work, Management of hot wor.question: 一名焊工正在封闭或受限区域内作业，或要紧密接触船只结构。如何针对接触船体或框架导致的触电风险为焊工提供附加的保护？
options: 提供干燥的绝缘垫片或垫板
穿着安全靴
穿棉质连身工作服
开始焊接之前用新鲜水冲刷该区域
CD0283 — Hot work, Management of hot wor.answer: 提供干燥的绝缘垫片或垫板

CD0285 — Enclosed space entry, Awareness.question: According to IMO guidelines, how much oxygen, by volume, is required for entry into an enclosed space?
Which one of the following statements best describes the use of a safety harness when going down into an enclosed space?
options: They should be worn whenever possible to save time in the event of an emergency.
They should not be worn, as they are only for rescue and may get caught on obstructions.
They need not be worn, provided they are available in the emergency headquarters.
They need not be worn, provided one is available onboard ship
CD0285 — Enclosed space entry, Awareness.answer: They should be worn whenever possible to save time in the event of an emergency.

CD0285 — Enclosed space entry, Awareness.question: What should you do if you start feeling tired, or ill, feel your eyes watering, or start developing a headache in an enclosed space?
options: Leave the space immediately, report the matter and seek medical attention
Leave the space, have a rest and some fresh air and then return
Try working on and see if you get better.
Mention it to a colleague, just in case.
CD0285 — Enclosed space entry, Awareness.answer: Leave the space immediately, report the matter and seek medical attention

CD0285 — Enclosed space entry, Awareness.question: If you are working as part of a team in an enclosed space and one of your colleagues starts acting as though they were drunk what should happen?
options: All the team should leave the space immediately and seek medical attention.
The person who appears drunk should be told to leave the space.
The person who appears drunk should be reported.
The person who appears drunk should be given plenty of water.
CD0285 — Enclosed space entry, Awareness.answer: All the team should leave the space immediately and seek medical attention.

CD0285 — Enclosed space entry, Awareness.question: If there is any doubt about toxic vapours remaining in an enclosed space, what particular additional precaution should be taken?
options: Breathing apparatus and suitable protective clothing should be worn.
Ventilation should be stopped to avoid spreading vapours.
Personal gas monitors must be used by all members of the team.
The time each person can spend in the space should be limited.
CD0285 — Enclosed space entry, Awareness.answer: Breathing apparatus and suitable protective clothing should be worn.

CD0285 — Enclosed space entry, Awareness.question: What percentage of the Occupational Exposure Limit (OEL) do the IMO say is safe before seafarers enter an enclosed space?
options: No more than 50%.
No more than 100%.
No more than 0.1%.
No more than 20%.
CD0285 — Enclosed space entry, Awareness.answer: No more than 50%.

CD0285 — Enclosed space entry, Awareness.question: What is the main role of the attendant outside an enclosed space?
options: To remain at the entrance to the space, keep in contact with those in the space, and raise the alarm if there are any signs of danger.
To be available to immediately go in and get anyone out if they become ill.
To close the entrance once the team have entered the space and open it up again once they are ready to leave.
To pass tools or cleaning materials down into the space and help remove any cargo residues.
CD0285 — Enclosed space entry, Awareness.answer: To remain at the entrance to the space, keep in contact with those in the space, and raise the alarm if there are any signs of danger.

CD0285 — Enclosed space entry, Awareness.question: If there is any doubt about pockets of flammable gas remaining in an enclosed space, what particular precaution should be taken?
options: Portable lights and other electrical equipment should be of a type approved for use in an explosive atmosphere.
No more than one person should enter the space at any time.
Personal gas monitors must be used by all members of the team.
Only 24 Volt hand lamps should be used.
CD0285 — Enclosed space entry, Awareness.answer: Portable lights and other electrical equipment should be of a type approved for use in an explosive atmosphere.

CD0285 — Enclosed space entry, Awareness.question: If you are given a respirator to wear in an enclosed space, but don't like wearing it whilst working, what can you do?
options: If it is part of the agreed safety procedures you must continue to wear it.
Take it off, and if there are no bad smells then it will be okay.
If your personal monitor says that the atmosphere is okay then you can take it off.
Take it off now and again for short periods.
CD0285 — Enclosed space entry, Awareness.answer: If it is part of the agreed safety procedures you must continue to wear it.

CD0285 — Enclosed space entry, Awareness.question: Vehicle and diesel engine exhausts can be the source for toxic gas. This gas is:
options: Carbon monoxide.
Nitrogen.
Hydrogen chloride.
Hydrogen sulphide.
CD0285 — Enclosed space entry, Awareness.answer: Carbon monoxide.

CD0285 — Enclosed space entry, Awareness.question: What is the maximum level of flammable gas allowed for safe entry into an enclosed space?
options: 1% of the lower flammable limit.
50% of the lower flammable limit
1% by volume.
10% of the lower flammable limit.
CD0285 — Enclosed space entry, Awareness.answer: 1% of the lower flammable limit.

CD0285 — Enclosed space entry, Awareness.question: If there is any doubt about pockets of gas or toxic cargo remains in an enclosed space, what precaution should be taken?
options: Breathing apparatus must be worn at all times.
Personal gas monitors must be used.
An EEBD should be used.
The time each person can spend in the space should be limited.
CD0285 — Enclosed space entry, Awareness.answer: Breathing apparatus must be worn at all times.

CD0285 — Enclosed space entry, Awareness.question: Under what circumstances should someone acting as the attendant at the entrance to an enclosed space go into that space?
options: Only when relieved of that duty and as part of an organised rescue team.
If called for by the persons in that space.
If the persons in the space get into any difficulty.
If they can do so and remain in sight of the entrance.
CD0285 — Enclosed space entry, Awareness.answer: Only when relieved of that duty and as part of an organised rescue team.

CD0285 — Enclosed space entry, Awareness.question: According to IMO guidelines, if the atmosphere in an enclosed space is suspect, then..
options: Entry should only be made for essential operation, further testing, safety of life or safety of the ship.
No entry is allowed under any circumstances.
Entry can only be made provided there is no flammable gas
Entry can only be made provided there is no toxic gas.
CD0285 — Enclosed space entry, Awareness.answer: Entry should only be made for essential operation, further testing, safety of life or safety of the ship.

CD0285 — Enclosed space entry, Awareness.question: Who can take part in enclosed space entries, rescues or act as an attendant at the entrance to an enclosed space?
options: Only those who have had specific enclosed space training and have taken part in enclosed space rescue training drills.
Anyone who has been trained how to wear SCBA.
Anyone who has had an onboard safety briefing for the work.
Anyone holding a certificate of competency.
CD0285 — Enclosed space entry, Awareness.answer: Only those who have had specific enclosed space training and have taken part in enclosed space rescue training drills.

CD0285 — Enclosed space entry, Awareness.question: Which one of the following statements best describes the term 'Occupational Exposure Limit' (OEL)?
options: It is a guide to safe exposure to toxic products, based on the amount of a given substance and the time in contact it.
It is a guide to safe exposure to toxic products, based only on the amount of a given substance present.
It is a guide to safe exposure to toxic products, based only on the time in contact with the substance.
It is a guide to safe exposure to harmful ultra violet (UV) rays when working on deck.
CD0285 — Enclosed space entry, Awareness.answer: It is a guide to safe exposure to toxic products, based on the amount of a given substance and the time in contact it.

CD0285 — Enclosed space entry, Awareness.question: How can the presence of toxic gasses in an enclosed space be detected?
options: Selective tests have to be carried out with knowledge of which toxic products have previously been in the space.
Test for oxygen. Provided there is enough oxygen, and no bad smells, the space should be safe.
Test for flammable gasses. If there are no flammable gasses and no bad smells, the space should be safe.
Use a personal monitor, calibrated for carbon monoxide or hydrogen sulphide.
CD0285 — Enclosed space entry, Awareness.answer: Selective tests have to be carried out with knowledge of which toxic products have previously been in the space.

CD0285 — Enclosed space entry, Awareness.question: Which one of the following statements best describes why a ship's chain locker should be classed as an enclosed space?
options: Because there is limited ventilation and rusting may use up the oxygen in the space.
Because it may be below the waterline.
Because it would be dangerous to be in there during anchoring operations.
Because access may be restricted.
CD0285 — Enclosed space entry, Awareness.answer: Because there is limited ventilation and rusting may use up the oxygen in the space.

CD0285 — Enclosed space entry, Awareness.question: Once an emergency team has been prepared for an enclosed space rescue, which one of these options is their first priority in most situations?
options: To supply the casualty with clean air and then get them out of the space and into fresh air.
To treat all of the casualty's injuries at the scene of the incident.
To find out the cause of the incident.
To see if they can get the casualty sufficiently recovered to avoid having to lift them out.
CD0285 — Enclosed space entry, Awareness.answer: To supply the casualty with clean air and then get them out of the space and into fresh air.

CD0285 — Enclosed space entry, Awareness.question: According to the IMO, which one of the following options best completes the following statement "an enclosed space is one which might have any of the following characteristics...
options: ... limited openings for entry and exit, inadequate ventilation or is not designed for continuous worker occupancy"
...is not open to the atmosphere or is used as a store ".
...has only one opening and is bounded by steel bulkheads and deckheads".
...is kept locked, with a warning sign posted".
CD0285 — Enclosed space entry, Awareness.answer: ... limited openings for entry and exit, inadequate ventilation or is not designed for continuous worker occupancy"

CD0285 — Enclosed space entry, Awareness.question: Which one of these statements best describes the effects some cargoes can have on the atmosphere in a cargo space?
options: They can use up or displace oxygen and give off toxic or flammable gasses.
Very little effect, since the spaces are ventilated.
The atmosphere can develop a bad smell.
No effect, because any harmful cargoes are sealed.
CD0285 — Enclosed space entry, Awareness.answer: They can use up or displace oxygen and give off toxic or flammable gasses.

CD0285 — Enclosed space entry, Awareness.question: Stagnant water, some sewage systems and some oil cargoes can all be the source for a gas which is both flammable and toxic. This gas is:
options: Hydrogen sulphide.
Nitrogen.
Hydrogen chloride.
Carbon dioxide.
CD0285 — Enclosed space entry, Awareness.answer: Hydrogen sulphide.

CD0285 — Enclosed space entry, Awareness.question: If you are working in an enclosed space and the attendant instructs you to leave, what should you do?
options: Leave the space immediately, and ensure the rest of the team does the same.
Check your personal gas monitor.
Ask why work is being stopped and contact the officer of the watch.
Ask for an SCBA to be brought in so that you can continue working.
CD0285 — Enclosed space entry, Awareness.answer: Leave the space immediately, and ensure the rest of the team does the same.

CD0285 — Enclosed space entry, Awareness.question: Which one of the following statements best describes why a ship's sewage tank should be classed as an enclosed space?
options: Because it is likely to contain toxic or flammable gasses.
Because it might be quite small and difficult to move around in.
Because it is a covered space.
Because it is inside the engine room.
CD0285 — Enclosed space entry, Awareness.answer: Because it is likely to contain toxic or flammable gasses.

CD0285 — Enclosed space entry, Awareness.question: Which one of the following options best completes the following statement?^M	"Onboard ship, an enclosed space is any space which...
options: ... has limited ventilation or could contain toxic or flammable vapours"
...is not open to the atmosphere".
...has four walls and a ceiling".
...has a danger sign at the entrance".
CD0285 — Enclosed space entry, Awareness.answer: ... has limited ventilation or could contain toxic or flammable vapours"

CD0285 — Enclosed space entry, Awareness.question: When should an Emergency Escape Breathing Device (EEBD) be used in an enclosed space?
options: Only as a means of escape when an unexpected hazard occurs.
It can be worn by a rescuer in an emergency.
It can be worn for short periods of work when toxic gasses are present
It can be worn for short periods of work when there is a lack of oxygen.
CD0285 — Enclosed space entry, Awareness.answer: Only as a means of escape when an unexpected hazard occurs.

CD0285 — Enclosed space entry, Awareness.question: Which one of the following statements best describes how enclosed space rescues should be organised?
options: All rescues should be by a team following pre-arranged procedures.
As speed is vital, the person nearest the space should attempt a quick rescue where possible.
If the casualties can be seen from the entrance to the space then the attendant should rescue them.
Senior officers should act on their own initiative.
CD0285 — Enclosed space entry, Awareness.answer: All rescues should be by a team following pre-arranged procedures.

CD0285 — Enclosed space entry, Awareness.question: Which one of the following options correctly completes the following statement?^M	"Before entry into any space which has limited ventilation or might contain toxic or flammable gasses...
options: …shipboard procedures, including risk assessment by a competent person, should be followed".
…the door should be left open for at least an hour".
…the ventilation fan should be run for at least two hours".
…you should let someone know where you are going".
CD0285 — Enclosed space entry, Awareness.answer: …shipboard procedures, including risk assessment by a competent person, should be followed".

CD0285 — Enclosed space entry, Awareness.question: When rusting of ship's steelwork occurs, which one of the following is the main effect on the air inside a ballast tank or cargo tank?
options: The oxygen content of the air decreases.
The oxygen content of the air increases.
The air develops a bad smell.
Carbon dioxide is given off by the rusting process.
CD0285 — Enclosed space entry, Awareness.answer: The oxygen content of the air decreases.

CD0285 — Enclosed space entry, Awareness.question: If the ventilation fails whilst you are working in an enclosed space, what should you do?
options: Leave the space immediately and ensure everyone else does the same
Carry on working as long as your gas alarm does not sound
Ensure someone is regularly checking the atmosphere
Report the ventilation failure, but carry on working if the atmosphere is still safe
CD0285 — Enclosed space entry, Awareness.answer: Leave the space immediately and ensure everyone else does the same

CD0286 — Crane operations, Heavy lift.question: Which one of the given options best completes the following statement? ‘If a heavy lift breaks its lashings in bad weather...
options: ...it is an extremely dangerous operation trying to re-fasten them’.
...just leave it till the weather dies down’.
...the company will not be very happy about it’.
...the vessel should return to port to get them re-attached’.
CD0286 — Crane operations, Heavy lift.answer: ...it is an extremely dangerous operation trying to re-fasten them’.

CD0286 — Crane operations, Heavy lift.question: Which one of the given options correctly describes why slack tanks should be avoided on a vessel when taking a heavy lift?
options: To stop the vessel’s effective GM being reduced.
To stop water or oil overflowing through air vents.
Because a liquid moving in a tank increases a vessel’s GM.
Because a liquid moving across a tank can damage it.
CD0286 — Crane operations, Heavy lift.answer: To stop the vessel’s effective GM being reduced.

CD0286 — Crane operations, Heavy lift.question: Select the one option which correctly identifies why some space is needed around a heavy load when it is stowed on a vessel.
options: To be able to work the lift safely.
To allow other cargo to be packed around it.
So that it does not touch the side of the vessel.
So there is a fire break in case of fire in the hold.
CD0286 — Crane operations, Heavy lift.answer: To be able to work the lift safely.

CD0286 — Crane operations, Heavy lift.question: Select the one option which correctly identifies the use of a chain register on a heavy lift cargo vessel.
options: The chain register is a list of cranes and lifting equipment.
The chain register is a certificate certifying the strength of the anchor chain.
The chain register is only a list of lifting slings used on a vessel.
The chain register is a list of chains used for lashing cargo.
CD0286 — Crane operations, Heavy lift.answer: The chain register is a list of cranes and lifting equipment.

CD0286 — Crane operations, Heavy lift.question: Select the one option which correctly identifies the markings seen on a crane, as required by a classification society.
options: The SWL and any limiting outreach values.
The name of the crane manufacturer.
The name of the classification society that issues the crane certificate.
The item number and the testing authority.
CD0286 — Crane operations, Heavy lift.answer: The SWL and any limiting outreach values.

CD0286 — Crane operations, Heavy lift.question: Select the one option which best completes the following statement. ‘When taking a heavy lift a vessel has to be securely moored...
options: ...to stop the suspended load moving relative to the quay’.
...to stop fender damage’.
...to reduce wear in the crane slewing bearing ’.
...to make it easier to take the lift’.
CD0286 — Crane operations, Heavy lift.answer: ...to stop the suspended load moving relative to the quay’.

CD0286 — Crane operations, Heavy lift.question: Select the one option which correctly identifies how the chain register requires lifting equipment to be marked.
options: Lifting equipment is to have the SWL, an identifying number and testing authority.
Lifting equipment is to have the SWL, maker and testing authority.
Lifting equipment is to have the SWL and identifying number.
Lifting equipment is to have the SWL, vessel’s name and testing authority.
CD0286 — Crane operations, Heavy lift.answer: Lifting equipment is to have the SWL, an identifying number and testing authority.

CD0286 — Crane operations, Heavy lift.question: Select the one option which correctly completes the following statement. ‘Any non tested loose gear on a heavy lift cargo vessel should...
options: ...be isolated and not used for lifting operations’.
...be kept with the other loose cargo gear’.
...be sent ashore permanently’.
...be sent ashore for testing and certification’.
CD0286 — Crane operations, Heavy lift.answer: ...be isolated and not used for lifting operations’.

CD0286 — Crane operations, Heavy lift.question: Select the one option which correctly identifies why all personnel involved in a heavy lift operation should be aware of the content of the lifting plan.
options: So that a cohesive team is formed to support each other.
So the lift supervisor has less to do when the lift is taking place.
So that team members can relieve each other to do other work.
To cover the insurance requirements for the lift
CD0286 — Crane operations, Heavy lift.answer: So that a cohesive team is formed to support each other.

CD0286 — Crane operations, Heavy lift.question: Select the one option which correctly completes the following statement. ‘Loose gear on a heavy lift vessel should be tested...
options: ...as thoroughly as the crane itself’.
...only by the supplier when new’.
...every month when the crane is tested’.
...to destruction to check the breaking load’.
CD0286 — Crane operations, Heavy lift.answer: ...as thoroughly as the crane itself’.

CD0286 — Crane operations, Heavy lift.question: Select the one option which correctly identifies why there is a limit on how short the legs in a multi leg lifting sling can be.
options: To minimise the horizontal force component in each leg when on a wide load.
To minimise the vertical force component on each leg when on a wide load.
So that the crane head does not have to be raised so far.
Because the longer the sling the weaker it will be.
CD0286 — Crane operations, Heavy lift.answer: To minimise the horizontal force component in each leg when on a wide load.

CD0286 — Crane operations, Heavy lift.question: Select the one option which is correct for the following statement. ‘The supervisor of a lifting operation should not appoint themselves as the crane signaler’.
options: The statement is correct, as the supervisor needs to keep an overview of an operation.
The statement is correct, as the supervisor will be on the vessel’s bridge not close to the crane.
The statement is incorrect, as the supervisor knows best what to do.
The statement is incorrect, as the supervisor is most experienced and should direct the crane.
CD0286 — Crane operations, Heavy lift.answer: The statement is correct, as the supervisor needs to keep an overview of an operation.

CD0286 — Crane operations, Heavy lift.question: Select the one option which correctly identifies which persons are qualified to drive a heavy lift crane on board a vessel.
options: Persons that have been trained and properly assessed as competent.
Crane drivers employed by stevedores.
Any of the crewmen with a bit of training are able to drive the crane.
Only the chief officer is allowed to drive the crane.
CD0286 — Crane operations, Heavy lift.answer: Persons that have been trained and properly assessed as competent.

CD0286 — Crane operations, Heavy lift.question: Select the one option which best describes the use of a ‘toolbox’ talk before or during an operation on a heavy lift vessel.
options: The team involved are briefed with the latest information.
It is a social get together in the deck workshop.
It is the management telling the team the lifting plan.
It is a discussion concerning tools to be used.
CD0286 — Crane operations, Heavy lift.answer: The team involved are briefed with the latest information.

CD0286 — Crane operations, Heavy lift.question: Select the one option which correctly describes a particular hazard associated with a tandem crane operation.
options: The crane heads can clash.
There could be a shortage of qualified crane drivers.
There may not be enough generating capacity on a vessel.
The load may become distorted.
CD0286 — Crane operations, Heavy lift.answer: The crane heads can clash.

CD0286 — Crane operations, Heavy lift.question: Select the one option which correctly identifies the function of a crane signaler.
options: A signaller directs the crane using a radio or hand signals.
A signaller only directs the crane when the crane driver cannot see the load.
A signaller is positioned close to the stowage position to give directions
A signaller is always positioned at the hatch coaming to observe the operation.
CD0286 — Crane operations, Heavy lift.answer: A signaller directs the crane using a radio or hand signals.

CD0286 — Crane operations, Heavy lift.question: Select the one option which best completes the following statement. ‘When taking a heavy lift on a vessel, company procedures...
options: ...should be followed at all times’.
...are unnecessary as personnel all know what to do’.
...do not cover the lifting operation’.
...are a not always relevant as they cannot be referenced on the deck of a vessel’.
CD0286 — Crane operations, Heavy lift.answer: ...should be followed at all times’.

CD0286 — Crane operations, Heavy lift.question: Select the one option which best identifies why a heavy lifting operation on a vessel should be individually risk assessed.
options: Because a heavy lift is a unique event, unlike everyday crane operations.
Because the heavy lift or vessel might be damaged.
Because generic crane risk assessments are poorly completed.
Because the warranty surveyor demands this action.
CD0286 — Crane operations, Heavy lift.answer: Because a heavy lift is a unique event, unlike everyday crane operations.

CD0286 — Crane operations, Heavy lift.question: Select the one option which correctly completes the following statement. ‘Loose gear on a heavy lift vessel is an expression given to...
options: ...equipment connecting the load to the crane hook’.
...cargo bearers surplus to requirements’.
...wires and blocks hanging from a crane structure’.
...spare luffing and lifting wires’.
CD0286 — Crane operations, Heavy lift.answer: ...equipment connecting the load to the crane hook’.

CD0286 — Crane operations, Heavy lift.question: Select the one option which correctly identifies the devices on a heavy lift crane that are required by a classification society to be tested daily when the crane is in use.
options: Audible alarms and holding capacity.
Vessel blackout.
Fire and gas alarm response.
Control system failure.
CD0286 — Crane operations, Heavy lift.answer: Audible alarms and holding capacity.

CD0286 — Crane operations, Heavy lift.question: Select the one option which best completes the following statement. ‘Risk assessment for a heavy lifting operation...
options: ...covers the vessel, cargo and personnel involved’.
...covers risks to the vessel only’.
...covers risks to the cargo only’.
...covers risks to the personnel involved only’.
CD0286 — Crane operations, Heavy lift.answer: ...covers the vessel, cargo and personnel involved’.

CD0286 — Crane operations, Heavy lift.question: Select the one option which best describes how the risk of crane malfunction is controlled on a heavy lift vessel.
options: Risk is controlled by correctly maintaining the crane.
It is controlled by having the technical superintendent organise crane maintenance schedules.
It is controlled by using the crane well within its SWL rating.
Risk is controlled by only using the crane in daylight hours.

检查油箱内的液压油位
CD0301 — Lifting operation, Safe use of.answer: 测试限位开关和急停装置是否运行正常

CD0301 — Lifting operation, Safe use of.question: Why should a sling always be attached above or symmetrical with a load’s centre of gravity? Select the BEST answer.
options: To stop the load tilting and sliding
Because this is what the lifting plan probably says
Because it looks better
To stop the load being damaged by bending
CD0301 — Lifting operation, Safe use of.answer: To stop the load tilting and sliding

CD0301 — Lifting operation, Safe use of.question: Почему стропы всегда должны крепиться над центром тяжести или симметрично по отношению к нему? Выберите НАИБОЛЕЕ ПОДХОДЯЩИЙ вариант ответа.
options: Чтобы предотвратить крен и волочение груза.
Так может быть указано в плане грузоподъемных работ.
Потому что это смотрится лучше.
Чтобы предотвратить повреждение груза из-за сгибания.
CD0301 — Lifting operation, Safe use of.answer: Чтобы предотвратить крен и волочение груза.

CD0301 — Lifting operation, Safe use of.question: 为什么吊索总是要位于荷载重心上方或对称于重心放置？ 请选择最佳答案。
options: 防止荷载倾斜和滑动
因为这可能是起重计划中的规定
因为这样看起来好些
防止荷载弯曲损坏
CD0301 — Lifting operation, Safe use of.answer: 防止荷载倾斜和滑动

CD0301 — Lifting operation, Safe use of.question: What markings are typically found on a service crane jib?
options: There will always be an indication of the Safe Working Load
There will always be information on the maximum slewing speed
It is very common not to see markings as they are painted out
Usually only a small maker’s plate
CD0301 — Lifting operation, Safe use of.answer: There will always be an indication of the Safe Working Load

CD0301 — Lifting operation, Safe use of.question: Какая маркировка обычно находится на стреле вспомогательного крана?
options: Всегда должна быть указана безопасная рабочая нагрузка.
Всегда должна быть информация о максимальной скорости поворота.
Очень часто маркировка закрашена, поэтому ее не видно.
Обычно это небольшая заводская табличка.
CD0301 — Lifting operation, Safe use of.answer: Всегда должна быть указана безопасная рабочая нагрузка.

CD0301 — Lifting operation, Safe use of.question: 一台服务起重机悬臂上通常带有哪些标记？
options: 通常标有安全作业荷载
通常带有最大回转速度信息
看不到这些标记的情况非常常见，因为是喷涂上去的
通常只是一个很小的制造商标牌
CD0301 — Lifting operation, Safe use of.answer: 通常标有安全作业荷载

CD0301 — Lifting operation, Safe use of.question: Is the following statement true or false? ‘Any crane can be used to transfer personnel in a man-riding basket.’
options: False
True

‘Yes, that’s correct! Man-riding baskets are a very common way to transfer personnel between vessels during an STS operation. They are also used in the offshore world. However, the crane ALWAYS has to be certified for this purpose and not all are.’
‘No, that is incorrect. Yes - a transfer basket can be attached and used on any crane hook, however personnel are the most precious cargo and the crane should ALWAYS be certified for man-riding.’
CD0301 — Lifting operation, Safe use of.answer: False

CD0301 — Lifting operation, Safe use of.question: Верно или неверно следующее утверждение? «Любой кран можно использовать для перемещения персонала в люльке».
options: Неверно
Верно

«Да, это правильный ответ. Люльки являются очень распространенным средством перемещения персонала с судна на судно. Они также используются на морских объектах. Однако кран ОБЯЗАТЕЛЬНО должен быть сертифицирован для такого применения, а такая сертификация есть не у всех кранов».

«Нет, это неправильный ответ. Транспортную люльку действительно можно прицепить к крюку любого крана, однако персонал является самым ценным грузом, поэтому кран ОБЯЗАТЕЛЬНО должен быть сертифицирован для перемещения людей».
CD0301 — Lifting operation, Safe use of.answer: Неверно

CD0301 — Lifting operation, Safe use of.question: 下面的陈述是真是假？ “任何起重机均可用于在载人篮中运送人员。”
options: 错误
正确
正确。这是正确选项！ 载人篮是 STS 作业期间在船舶之间运送人员的一种非常常见的方式。载人篮还会用于海上。但是，起重机务必经过认证才能用于该用途，并非所有起重机均可用于此用途。
不正确。是的 - 任何起重机吊钩上均可连接和使用输送篮，但是人是最贵重的货物，起重机务必要经过认证才能用于载人。
CD0301 — Lifting operation, Safe use of.answer: 错误

CD0301 — Lifting operation, Safe use of.question: Is the following statement true or false? ‘A routine lifting operation does not normally require a signaller.’
options: False
True
Yes, that’s correct! A crewmember should always be in place to signal to the crane driver.
No, that’s incorrect! Even for the simplest lift a crewmember should always be in place to signal to the crane driver.
CD0301 — Lifting operation, Safe use of.answer: False

CD0301 — Lifting operation, Safe use of.question: Верно или неверно следующее утверждение? Для обычной грузоподъемной операции, как правило, не требуется сигнальщик.
options: Неверно
Верно
Да, это правильный ответ. На месте всегда должен присутствовать член экипажа, подающий сигналы крановщику.
Нет, это неправильный ответ. Даже при простейшей грузоподъемной операции всегда должен присутствовать член экипажа, подающий сигналы крановщику.
CD0301 — Lifting operation, Safe use of.answer: Неверно

CD0301 — Lifting operation, Safe use of.question: 下面的陈述是真是假？ “常规起重作业通常不需要信号员。”
options: 错误
正确
正确。这是正确选项！ 务必存在一名船员向起重机驾驶员发出信号。
不正确！ 即使最简单的起重，也务必存在一名船员向起重机驾驶员发出信号。
CD0301 — Lifting operation, Safe use of.answer: 错误

CD0302 — Permit to work.question: 如果作业期间许可上规定的一个条件无法遵循，应该采取什么措施？ 请选择一个正确答案。

CD0302 — Permit to work.question: Какое действие следует предпринять, если в ходе работы невозможно соблюсти одно из условий, указанных в допуске? Выберите ОДИН правильный вариант ответа.

Прекратить работу и поставить в известность лицо, выдавшее допуск.
Продолжить работу и провести новую оценку рисков.

CD0302 — Permit to work.question: Quale azione si deve intraprendere se, mentre è in corso il lavoro, emerge che una delle condizioni specificate nell'autorizzazione non può essere rispettata? Selezioni l'UNICA risposta esatta.

CD0302 — Permit to work.question: Почему следует хранить на борту допуски и связанные с ними документы? Выберите ОДИН ПРАВИЛЬНЫЙ вариант ответа.

CD0302 — Permit to work.answer: Они требуются во время проверок в соответствии с Международным кодексом по управлению безопасностью, при аудиторских проверках и расследовании происшествий.

CD0302 — Permit to work.question: Perché le autorizzazioni e gli altri documenti a esse connessi devono essere conservati a bordo? Selezioni l'UNICA risposta ESATTA.

CD0303 — COLREGs, Lights, shapes and sou.answer: One long followed by two short blasts on the whistle every two minutes.

CD0303 — COLREGs, Lights, shapes and sou.question: A vessel is proceeding along a narrow channel and hears the following signal “two long blasts and two short blasts on a whistle” from astern. How should the vessel respond?
options: The response should be one long, one short, one long and one short blast on the whistle, if in agreement to be overtaken.
The response should be two long blasts and two short blasts on the whistle if in agreement to overtaken on the port side.
The response should be one long, one short, one long and one short blast on the whistle.
The response is one long blast on the whistle if  not in agreement to be overtaken.
CD0303 — COLREGs, Lights, shapes and sou.answer: The response should be one long, one short, one long and one short blast on the whistle, if in agreement to be overtaken.

CD0303 — COLREGs, Lights, shapes and sou.question: Which fog signal should a sailing vessel sound in reduced visibility?
options: One long blast followed by two short blasts on the whistle every two minutes.
One long blast on the whistle every two minutes.
Two long blasts on the whistle every two minutes.
Four short blasts on the whistle every two minutes.
CD0303 — COLREGs, Lights, shapes and sou.answer: One long blast followed by two short blasts on the whistle every two minutes.

CD0303 — COLREGs, Lights, shapes and sou.question: What is understood by the term “prolonged blast”?
options: A blast of from four to six seconds in duration.
A blast of about one second in duration.
A blast of about two seconds in duration.
A blast of about three seconds in duration.
CD0303 — COLREGs, Lights, shapes and sou.answer: A blast of from four to six seconds in duration.

CD0303 — COLREGs, Lights, shapes and sou.question: Which fog signal should a vessel restricted in her ability to manoeuvre, sound in reduced visibility?
options: One long followed by two short blasts on the whistle every two minutes.
One long blast on the whistle every two minutes.
Two long blasts on the whistle every two minutes.
Four short blasts on the whistle every two minutes.
CD0303 — COLREGs, Lights, shapes and sou.answer: One long followed by two short blasts on the whistle every two minutes.

CD0303 — COLREGs, Lights, shapes and sou.question: What manoeuvring signal would a power-driven vessel give to another vessel when they are in sight of each other, when going astern on the engines?”
options: Three short blasts on the whistle.
One short blast on the whistle.
Two short blasts on the whistle.
Five short and rapid blasts on the whistle.
CD0303 — COLREGs, Lights, shapes and sou.answer: Three short blasts on the whistle.

CD0303 — COLREGs, Lights, shapes and sou.question: A vessel is seen showing a black ball in the fore part of the vessel. What does this day time signal indicate?
options: It is a ship at anchor.
It is a cable-laying vessel.
It is a vessel that has run aground.
It is a ship that it is showing that it is “under way” but not making any way through the water.
CD0303 — COLREGs, Lights, shapes and sou.answer: It is a ship at anchor.

CD0303 — COLREGs, Lights, shapes and sou.question: A vessel is seen showing a white light in the fore part of the vessel. What does this night time signal indicate?
options: It is a ship at anchor, under 50 metres in length.
It is a cable-laying vessel.
It is a vessel that has run aground under 100 metres in length.
It is a ship that it is showing that it is “under way” but not making any way through the water.
CD0303 — COLREGs, Lights, shapes and sou.answer: It is a ship at anchor, under 50 metres in length.

CD0303 — COLREGs, Lights, shapes and sou.question: What manoeuvring signal would a power-driven vessel give to another vessel when they are in sight of each other, when altering course to port?”
options: Two short blasts.
One short blast.
Three short blasts.
A minimum of five short blasts.
CD0303 — COLREGs, Lights, shapes and sou.answer: Two short blasts.

CD0303 — COLREGs, Lights, shapes and sou.question: Which fog signal should a vessel not under command, sound in reduced visibility?
options: One long followed by two short blasts on the whistle every two minutes.
One long blast on the whistle every two minutes.
Two long blasts on the whistle every two minutes.
Four short blasts on the whistle every two minutes.
CD0303 — COLREGs, Lights, shapes and sou.answer: One long followed by two short blasts on the whistle every two minutes.

CD0303 — COLREGs, Lights, shapes and sou.question: What is the fog signal for a power driven vessel engaged in pushing another vessel ahead, but not as a composite unit?
options: One long blast followed by two short blasts every two minutes.
Two short blasts and one long every one minute.
One long blast every two minute.
Two short blasts followed by one long blast every two minutes.
CD0303 — COLREGs, Lights, shapes and sou.answer: One long blast followed by two short blasts every two minutes.

CD0303 — COLREGs, Lights, shapes and sou.question: What is the fog signal for a power driven vessel engaged in towing another vessel?
options: One long blast followed by two short blasts every two minutes.
Two short blasts and one long every one minute.
One long blast every two minute.
Two short blasts followed by one long blast every two minutes.
CD0303 — COLREGs, Lights, shapes and sou.answer: One long blast followed by two short blasts every two minutes.

CD0303 — COLREGs, Lights, shapes and sou.question: What is the daytime signal of a vessel aground? Select the ONE correct answer.
options: Three black balls in a vertical line, where they can best be seen.
Two black balls in a vertical line, where they can best be seen and in addition, the anchor ball forward.
The black cylinder where it can best be seen.
The anchor lights for a vessel of its size and also two all round red lights where they can best be seen.
CD0303 — COLREGs, Lights, shapes and sou.answer: Three black balls in a vertical line, where they can best be seen.

CD0303 — COLREGs, Lights, shapes and sou.question: A vessel is showing three lights in a vertical line, upper and lower red and the middle one white. She also shows two white mast head lights, side lights and stern light. Which ONE of the following answers best describes this vessel?
options: A vessel restricted in her ability to manoeuvre, underway and making way through the water.
A vessel restricted in her ability to manoeuvre underway, but it is unknown if making way through the water, or not.
A vessel not under command and still moving through the water.
A vessel engaged in dredging, under way and making way though the water.
CD0303 — COLREGs, Lights, shapes and sou.answer: A vessel restricted in her ability to manoeuvre, underway and making way through the water.

CD0303 — COLREGs, Lights, shapes and sou.question: What is the fog signal of a fishing vessel not engaged in fishing? Select the ONE correct answer.
options: The normal fog signal for a power driven vessel of her size
The fog signal one long blast followed by two short blasts
The fog signal one long blast followed by three short blasts
The fog signal one long blast followed by four short blasts
CD0303 — COLREGs, Lights, shapes and sou.answer: The normal fog signal for a power driven vessel of her size

CD0303 — COLREGs, Lights, shapes and sou.question: The two white mast head lights of a vessel are seen by another ship. What is the length of this vessel? Select the ONE correct answer.
options: Any length – the length is unknown
Two mast head lights indicate the length is over 50 metres.
The vessel is over 100 metres in length
The vessel is under 100 metres in length.
CD0303 — COLREGs, Lights, shapes and sou.answer: Any length – the length is unknown

CD0303 — COLREGs, Lights, shapes and sou.question: What is the night time signal that may be displayed by a vessel to indicate she is constrained by her draught? Select the ONE correct answer.
options: Normal steaming lights of a power driven vessel of her size and in addition three all round red lights in a vertical line where they can best be seen.
Normal steaming lights of a power driven vessel of her size and in addition two all round red lights in a vertical line where they can best be seen.
Normal steaming lights of a power driven vessel of her size and in addition a black cylinder, where it can best be seen.
Normal steaming lights of a power driven vessel of her size and in addition three all round lights, the upper and lower red and the middle one white, in a vertical line where they can best be seen.
CD0303 — COLREGs, Lights, shapes and sou.answer: Normal steaming lights of a power driven vessel of her size and in addition three all round red lights in a vertical line where they can best be seen.

CD0304 — COLREGs, Conduct of vessels.question: A vessel is observed approaching from the port side showing two black balls. A series of bearings indicate that a close quarter situation is likely to occur. As Officer of the Watch, indicate what action should be taken within the meaning of the Rules.
options: Take early and substantial action to keep well clear.
It would be expected that the vessel will be slowing down and therefore no action should be necessary.
Give two short blasts on the whistle and alter course to port.
Maintain your course and speed.
CD0304 — COLREGs, Conduct of vessels.answer: Take early and substantial action to keep well clear.

CD0304 — COLREGs, Conduct of vessels.question: You are Officer of the Watch on a vessel when you observe another two vessels crossing from port. Both of these vessels are showing a black diamond and one is also showing three shapes, the highest and lowest are black balls and the middle one a black diamond. What would be the most suitable initial action to be taken by your vessel under these Rules, if the bearing of the nearest vessel is only changing slowly?
options: Slow down your vessel and allow the two vessels to pass ahead.
Maintain your course and speed as the vessels are crossing from port.
Sound one short blast and make a series of small alterations of course to starboard.
Maintain your course and speed until you are close to the other vessel, in case it makes an alteration of course.
CD0304 — COLREGs, Conduct of vessels.answer: Slow down your vessel and allow the two vessels to pass ahead.

CD0304 — COLREGs, Conduct of vessels.question: A vessel is observed approaching from the port side, showing two red lights and also a green side light.  A series of bearings indicate that a close quarter situation is likely to occur.  As Officer of the Watch, indicate what action should be taken within the meaning of the Rules.
options: Take early and substantial action to keep well clear.
It would be expected that the vessel will be slowing down and therefore no action should be necessary.
Give two short blasts on the whistle and alter course to port.
Maintain your course and speed.
CD0304 — COLREGs, Conduct of vessels.answer: Take early and substantial action to keep well clear.

CD0304 — COLREGs, Conduct of vessels.question: You are bridge Officer of the Watch in poor visibility and plot another vessel on the radar approaching your ship from the port side so as to involve a close quarter situation. Which of the following is the most suitable action required under these Rules?
options: Make an early and substantial alteration of course to starboard.
Make an early and substantial alteration of course to port.
Maintain your course and speed as the “stand-on” vessel.
Make a small reduction in speed to allow the other vessel to pass ahead.
CD0304 — COLREGs, Conduct of vessels.answer: Make an early and substantial alteration of course to starboard.

CD0304 — COLREGs, Conduct of vessels.question: As Officer of the Watch you sight another power driven vessel on the port side approaching your vessel on a collision course. Which ONE of the following answers is the correct initial responsibility under the Rules?
options: Your vessel should maintain its speed and course.
Your vessel is obliged to keep out of the way of the other vessel therefore you alter your course to the starboard.
Your vessel is obliged to keep out of the way of the other vessel therefore you alter your course to the port.
Your vessel is obliged to keep out of the way of the other vessel therefore you should slow down and allow the other vessel to pass ahead.
CD0304 — COLREGs, Conduct of vessels.answer: Your vessel should maintain its speed and course.

CD0304 — COLREGs, Conduct of vessels.question: You are bridge Officer of the Watch and observe another vessel approaching from the port side across your course line, showing a red light over a white light and another white light on its starboard side and also a green side light. What would be the correct action to be taken by your vessel, if a close quarter situation is developing?
options: Take early and substantial action to keep well clear.
Maintain your course and speed for a crossing vessel from port.
Sound one short blast and alter course to port.
Sound two short blasts and alter course to starboard.
CD0304 — COLREGs, Conduct of vessels.answer: Take early and substantial action to keep well clear.

CD0304 — COLREGs, Conduct of vessels.question: You are Officer of the Watch on a vessel when you observe another two vessels crossing from port. Both of these vessels are showing a black diamond. What would be the correct initial action to be taken by your vessel under these Rules, if the bearing of the nearest vessel is only changing slowly?
options: Maintain your course and speed and continually monitor the situation.
Slow down your vessel and allow the two vessels to pass ahead.
Sound one short blast and alter your course to the starboard.
Sound two short blasts and alter course to port.
CD0304 — COLREGs, Conduct of vessels.answer: Maintain your course and speed and continually monitor the situation.

CD0304 — COLREGs, Conduct of vessels.question: As Officer of the Watch you sight another power driven vessel on the starboard side approaching your vessel on a collision course. Which ONE of the following answers is the correct initial action to be taken under the Rules?
options: Take early and substantial action to keep well clear.
Maintain your course and speed.
Sound two short blasts on the whistle and alter course to port.
Make an early and substantial alteration of course to starboard.
CD0304 — COLREGs, Conduct of vessels.answer: Take early and substantial action to keep well clear.

CD0304 — COLREGs, Conduct of vessels.question: A bearing is taken of an approaching vessel and shortly afterwards another observation is made of the same vessel. The bearing is changing slowly, but under what circumstances (as defined in the Rules) could there still be a risk of a collision in this situation? Select the ONE best answer.
options: All of the suggested answers.
When approaching a very large vessel.
When approaching a vessel at close range.
When approaching a vessel engaged in towing.
CD0304 — COLREGs, Conduct of vessels.answer: All of the suggested answers.

CD0304 — COLREGs, Conduct of vessels.question: You are Officer of the Watch of a power driven vessel and your vessel is proceeding in fog, when you hear the fog signal of another power driven somewhere ahead of you. The signals seem to be getting closer, but nothing is detected on the radar. How should you proceed within the meaning of these rules?
options: Reduce the speed to lowest manoeuvring speed and if necessary take all the way off and proceed with extreme caution.
Slow down and proceed with caution.
Slow down, keep a sharp lookout and change the fog signal to two long blasts.
Stop the vessel and sound one long blast followed by two short blasts.
CD0304 — COLREGs, Conduct of vessels.answer: Reduce the speed to lowest manoeuvring speed and if necessary take all the way off and proceed with extreme caution.

CD0304 — COLREGs, Conduct of vessels.question: The visibility is about one mile and as Officer of the Watch you visually see a vessel dead ahead on a reciprocal course coming out of the fog towards you. What should be the action to take?
options: Give one short blast and make a substantial alteration of course to starboard.
Stop your vessel and change the fog signal to two long blasts every two minutes until the vessel has passed.
Alter course to starboard and continue sounding the fog signal, but do not sound one short blast, as this is for clear visibility only.
Maintain your course and speed.
CD0304 — COLREGs, Conduct of vessels.answer: Give one short blast and make a substantial alteration of course to starboard.

CD0304 — COLREGs, Conduct of vessels.question: Another vessel is observed dead ahead, steaming in the opposite direction. What action would the Officer of the Watch expect from the other vessel?
options: Expect the other vessel to alter its course to the starboard.
Expect the other vessel to alter its course to the port.
Expect the other vessel to maintain their course and speed.
Expect the other vessel to slow down.
CD0304 — COLREGs, Conduct of vessels.answer: Expect the other vessel to alter its course to the starboard.

CD0304 — COLREGs, Conduct of vessels.question: As Officer of the Watch you sight another power driven vessel on the port side approaching your vessel on a collision course. Which ONE of the following answers is the correct action under the Rules if the other vessel appears to be taking no action to avoid a close quarter situation?
options: You give a signal to the approaching vessel consisting of at least five short and rapid blasts combined with a light signal and keep monitoring the situation.
You give a signal to the approaching vessel consisting of two short blasts combined with a light signal and altering your course to the port.
You give a signal to the approaching vessel consisting of one short blast combined with a light signal and altering your course to the starboard.
You slow down and let the other vessel pass ahead.
CD0304 — COLREGs, Conduct of vessels.answer: You give a signal to the approaching vessel consisting of at least five short and rapid blasts combined with a light signal and keep monitoring the situation.

CD0304 — COLREGs, Conduct of vessels.question: As Officer of the watch of a power driven vessel, what should you take into consideration when entering a narrow channel?
options: Proceed at a safe speed, keeping to the starboard side of the fairway.
Reduce speed to a speed just enough to maintain steerage.
Be prepared to reduce your speed and keep to the starboard side of the fairway.
Proceed with great care and keep to the port side of the fairway.
CD0304 — COLREGs, Conduct of vessels.answer: Proceed at a safe speed, keeping to the starboard side of the fairway.

CD0304 — COLREGs, Conduct of vessels.question: You are Officer of the Watch on a vessel meeting another vessel in clear visibility on a collision course and you are the “give way” vessel. Under the Rules what action should you take to avoid a close quarter situation?
options: You should take early and substantial action to keep well clear.
You take whatever action is necessary to avoid a collision.
You should avoid a collision by sounding one short blast and altering course to starboard.
You should avoid a collision by altering course to port and giving two short blasts, under these Rules.
CD0304 — COLREGs, Conduct of vessels.answer: You should take early and substantial action to keep well clear.

CD0304 — COLREGs, Conduct of vessels.question: You are bridge Officer of the Watch and observe another vessel approaching from the port side across your course line and showing two black cones, points together and a cone point upwards on its starboard side. What would be the correct action to be taken by your vessel, if a close quarter situation is developing?
options: Take early and substantial action to keep well clear.
Maintain your course and speed for a crossing vessel from port.
Sound one short blast and alter course to port.
Sound two short blasts and alter course to starboard.
CD0304 — COLREGs, Conduct of vessels.answer: Take early and substantial action to keep well clear.

CD0304 — COLREGs, Conduct of vessels.question: You are Officer of the Watch on a vessel when you observe another vessel under full sail showing a black cone apex downwards and on a constant bearing of about 50 degrees on your port bow. What would be the correct initial action to be taken by your vessel?
options: Maintain your course and speed.
Alter your course to the port and sound two short blasts on the whistle.
Alter your course to the starboard and sound one short blast on the whistle.
Reduce your speed until the other vessel has passed ahead.
CD0304 — COLREGs, Conduct of vessels.answer: Maintain your course and speed.

CD0304 — COLREGs, Conduct of vessels.question: You are Officer of the Watch on a power driven vessel in a Traffic Separation Scheme and sight a fishing vessel engaged in fishing inside the Traffic Separation Scheme? Who has the responsibility to keep clear?
options: A vessel engaged in fishing shall not impede the passage of any vessel following a traffic lane.
A power driven vessel should keep clear of a vessel engaged in fishing.
A fishing vessel is not allowed to fish within the Traffic separation Scheme and should be forced to leave the area.
Your vessel is in the Traffic Separation Scheme and therefore does not need to keep clear of other vessels.
CD0304 — COLREGs, Conduct of vessels.answer: A vessel engaged in fishing shall not impede the passage of any vessel following a traffic lane.

CD0304 — COLREGs, Conduct of vessels.question: Are there any particular rules for sailing vessels and vessels less than 20 metres in length, when they are proceeding in a narrow channel?
options: They should not impede the passage of a vessel that can only safely navigate within a narrow channel of fairway.
They should always stop and allow larger vessels to pass in the narrow channel.
They should always keep to the port side in a narrow channel.
They should not pass a vessel that can only safely navigate within a narrow channel of fairway.
CD0304 — COLREGs, Conduct of vessels.answer: They should not impede the passage of a vessel that can only safely navigate within a narrow channel of fairway.

CD0304 — COLREGs, Conduct of vessels.question: What manoeuvring signal would a power-driven vessel give to another vessel when they are in sight of each other, when altering course to starboard?
options: One short blast.
Two short blasts.
Three short blasts.
A minimum of five short blasts.
CD0304 — COLREGs, Conduct of vessels.answer: One short blast.

CD0304 — COLREGs, Conduct of vessels.question: You are Officer of the Watch of a power driven vessel when your vessel encounters fog during your watch. What are the important initial actions that should be taken under these Rules?
options: All of the suggested answers.
Call the Master.
Ring Standby on the engines and reduce the speed to a safe speed as soon as possible.
Start sounding the appropriate fog signal.
CD0304 — COLREGs, Conduct of vessels.answer: All of the suggested answers.

CD0304 — COLREGs, Conduct of vessels.question: You are Officer of the Watch proceeding on your voyage in bad visibility. You have plotted a target on the radar screen and see that it is a ship on a collision course. What are the recommended actions to be taken in this situation?
options: All of the suggested answers.
Take action in ample time and avoid a series of small alterations.
Avoid an alteration to port for a vessel forward of the beam, other than for a vessel being overtaken.
Avoid an alteration of course towards a vessel abeam or abaft the beam.
CD0304 — COLREGs, Conduct of vessels.answer: All of the suggested answers.

CD0304 — COLREGs, Conduct of vessels.question: You are on a power driven vessel approaching the vessel illustrated (showing one black ball), directly ahead on your course line. What is the correct action to be taken by your vessel?
options: Taking into account any navigational hazards, take early and substantial action to keep well clear.
Taking into account any navigational hazards, you should adjust your course to avoid passing ahead of the other vessel.
Taking into account any navigational hazards alter course to starboard.
Slow down and allow the other vessel to pass clear of your vessel.
CD0304 — COLREGs, Conduct of vessels.answer: Taking into account any navigational hazards, take early and substantial action to keep well clear.

CD0304 — COLREGs, Conduct of vessels.question: You are on a power driven vessel approaching the vessel illustrated (showing two white lights), directly ahead on your course line. What is the correct action to be taken by your vessel?
options: Taking into account any navigational hazards, take early and substantial action to keep well clear.
Taking into account any navigational hazards, you should adjust your course to avoid passing ahead of the other vessel.
Taking into account any navigational hazards alter course to starboard.
Slow down and allow the other vessel to pass clear of your vessel.
CD0304 — COLREGs, Conduct of vessels.answer: Taking into account any navigational hazards, take early and substantial action to keep well clear.

CD0304 — COLREGs, Conduct of vessels.question: Which of the following statements is correct within the Rules?
options: You should join a traffic separation system at as small angle to the general direction of traffic flow as practicable.
It is important that all vessels in a traffic separation system keep the same speed.
You can enter a traffic separation only at the end points.
You are not allowed to fish in a traffic separation area.
CD0304 — COLREGs, Conduct of vessels.answer: You should join a traffic separation system at as small angle to the general direction of traffic flow as practicable.

CD0304 — COLREGs, Conduct of vessels.question: Which vessels are allowed to use an inshore traffic lane of a Traffic Separation Scheme?
options: All of the suggested options.
A vessel shorter than 20 metres.
Sailing vessels.
Vessels engaged in fishing.
CD0304 — COLREGs, Conduct of vessels.answer: All of the suggested options.

CD0304 — COLREGs, Conduct of vessels.question: A power driven vessel is sighted coming towards your ship from 45 degrees on the port side. The bearing is not changing and it is getting closer and appears to be taking no action. You have sounded five or more short and rapid blasts and it still appears to be taking no action. As “stand-on” vessel can you take action under the rules at this time?
options: Your vessel may take action to avoid collision by her manoeuvre alone, as soon as it becomes apparent to you that the vessel required to keep out of the way is not taking appropriate action.
You must take substantial action altering your course to the port and give two short blasts.
You must take substantial action, and give one short blast and change your course to the starboard.
You must take substantial action and give two short blasts and change your course to the starboard.
CD0304 — COLREGs, Conduct of vessels.answer: Your vessel may take action to avoid collision by her manoeuvre alone, as soon as it becomes apparent to you that the vessel required to keep out of the way is not taking appropriate action.

CD0304 — COLREGs, Conduct of vessels.question: Your vessel is a deep draught vessel and is approaching the entrance to a narrow channel. How should you proceed? Select the ONE best answer.
options: Reduce to a safe speed, keep a sharp lookout and keep to the starboard side of the fairway.
Reduce the speed and keep in the centre of the channel for maximum depth.
Reduce your speed and keep a sharp lookout.
Engines on standby ready to reduce your speed when required and stay to the starboard side of the fairway.
CD0304 — COLREGs, Conduct of vessels.answer: Reduce to a safe speed, keep a sharp lookout and keep to the starboard side of the fairway.

CD0304 — COLREGs, Conduct of vessels.question: Under what circumstances should a vessel consider itself to be an overtaking vessel within the meaning of the Rules? Select the ONE best answer.
options: A vessel is overtaking when coming up with another vessel from a direction more than 22.5 degrees abaft her beam or if in any doubt she shall assume that she is.
When you are faster than the other vessel.
When you are overtaking the other vessel from a direction more than 20 degrees abaft her beam.
When you are overtaking the other vessel from abaft her beam.
CD0304 — COLREGs, Conduct of vessels.answer: A vessel is overtaking when coming up with another vessel from a direction more than 22.5 degrees abaft her beam or if in any doubt she shall assume that she is.

CD0304 — COLREGs, Conduct of vessels.question: You are Officer of the Watch and see another vessel displaying two cones, points together and a cone point up on one side. This vessel is sighted dead ahead and the bearing is not altering. What actions should be taken?
options: Take early and substantial action to keep well clear of the other vessel.
You give it right of way and alter your course to best keep to your track.
The other vessel should give way to your vessel.
Sound not less than five short and rapid blasts on the whistle.
CD0304 — COLREGs, Conduct of vessels.answer: Take early and substantial action to keep well clear of the other vessel.

CD0304 — COLREGs, Conduct of vessels.question: A power driven vessel is sighted coming towards own ship from 45 degrees on the port side at a distance of two nautical miles and the bearing is still not changing. What is the first action you should take?
options: There is a close quarter situation developing and the other vessel is not keeping clear, therefore I would sound at least 5 short and rapid blasts to indicate my concern and monitor the situation.
There is a close quarter situation developing, but I am the “give way” vessel and therefore I shall keep well clear of the other ship.
There is a close quarter situation developing and the other vessel is the “keep clear” vessel, therefore I should maintain my speed and course.
There is a close quarter situation developing and under the Rules both vessels should give way to the other.
CD0304 — COLREGs, Conduct of vessels.answer: There is a close quarter situation developing and the other vessel is not keeping clear, therefore I would sound at least 5 short and rapid blasts to indicate my concern and monitor the situation.

CD0304 — COLREGs, Conduct of vessels.question: Your vessel is approaching a bend in a narrow channel with an obstructed view ahead. How should you proceed?
options: All of the suggested answers.
Proceed at a safe speed.
Sound one long blast.
Keep to the starboard side of the fairway.
CD0304 — COLREGs, Conduct of vessels.answer: All of the suggested answers.

CD0304 — COLREGs, Conduct of vessels.question: You are on a vessel approaching a Traffic Separation Scheme and wish to enter a port within the inshore traffic zone on the side of the Scheme which is used by vessels coming in the opposite direction. What is the correct approach to safely gain entry into the destination port in compliance with the Rules?
options: Take the “inshore traffic zone” and keep out of the main lanes of the scheme.
Enter the scheme in the correct main lane and at the appropriate position alter hard over and cross the other lane on a course at right angles to the main traffic flow.
Take the correct main lane until the end of the scheme and then return down the other lane until arriving at the appropriate position to exit for the destination.
Enter the scheme into the correct main lane and cross over the scheme at as small an angle as possible to the general direction of traffic flow.
CD0304 — COLREGs, Conduct of vessels.answer: Take the “inshore traffic zone” and keep out of the main lanes of the scheme.

CD0304 — COLREGs, Conduct of vessels.question: A power driven vessel is sighted coming towards your ship from 45 degrees on the port side, at a distance of five nautical miles and the bearing is not changing. What is the initial action you should take?
options: There is a risk of a close quarter situation, but the other ship is the “give way” ship, so I should maintain my course and speed, but monitor the situation.
There is a risk of a close quarter situation, but I am the “give way” vessel and therefore I shall keep well clear of the other ship.
There is no risk of a close quarter situation and therefore I should maintain my speed and course.
There is a risk of a close quarter situation and therefore both vessels should give way to each other.
CD0304 — COLREGs, Conduct of vessels.answer: There is a risk of a close quarter situation, but the other ship is the “give way” ship, so I should maintain my course and speed, but monitor the situation.

CD0304 — COLREGs, Conduct of vessels.question: You are Officer of the Watch proceeding in fog and hear one long blast every two minutes coming from ahead by a vessel approaching, which you have been tracking on your ARPA. You know that there is a risk of a close quarter situation. What would be the best action to take?
options: You should take avoiding action in goog time, avoiding an alteration to port.
You reduce your speed to a minimum manoeuvring speed, navigate with extreme caution and keep your engines ready to stop.
You should alter your course 15 degrees to the starboard.
You should make a series of small alterations to starboard.
CD0304 — COLREGs, Conduct of vessels.answer: You should take avoiding action in goog time, avoiding an alteration to port.

CD0304 — COLREGs, Conduct of vessels.question: Would a “safe speed” in restricted visibility, always be considered faster when a vessel has an operational ARPA radar, than on a vessel without a radar? Select the ONE best answer.
options: Not always, it may even be slower.
Yes, always faster on a vessel with an ARPA
The speed should be the same in both cases
It would never be faster just because the ship has an ARPA

CD0307 — Incident investigation, Investi.question: Vous enquêtez sur un incident qui a impliqué la rupture d'un câble sur un treuil d'amarrage et vous recueillez des preuves photographiques. CD0307 — Incident investigation, Investi.question: Si sta conducendo un'inchiesta su un incidente causato dalla rottura del cavo di un verricello da tonneggio, che comporta l'acquisizione di prove fotografiche. Dove cercherebbe di fotografare il cavo? Selezionare UNA SOLA risposta.

CD0307 — Incident investigation, Investi.question: What is the purpose of investigating incidents and using the knowledge gained from the investigation? Select the ONE best answer.

CD0307 — Incident investigation, Investi.question: 调查事件的目的，以及使用从调查获取的信息的目的是什么？ 请选择一个最佳答案。

CD0307 — Incident investigation, Investi.question: ¿Cuál es la finalidad de investigar los incidentes y del uso de los conocimientos adquiridos gracias a la investigación? Seleccione LA mejor respuesta.
options: Una reducción, o incluso eliminación, de dichos incidentes en el futuro
Una mayor probabilidad de que se produzcan estos incidentes en el futuro
Una reducción de las lesiones personales, pero un incremento de los incidentes con daños materiales
El desarrollo de un sistema más eficiente para establecer las culpas
CD0307 — Incident investigation, Investi.answer: Una reducción, o incluso eliminación, de dichos incidentes en el futuro

CD0307 — Incident investigation, Investi.question: Quel est l'objectif des enquêtes sur les incidents et de l'utilisation des enseignements tirés des enquêtes ? Sélectionnez une SEULE réponse, selon celle qui vous semble la meilleure.
options: Une diminution, voire l'élimination de tels incidents à l'avenir.

CD0307 — Incident investigation, Investi.question: Qual è lo scopo di svolgere inchieste su un incidente e di utilizzare le informazioni raccolte in questo modo? Selezionare UNA SOLA risposta.

Aumentare le probabilità che eventi analoghi si ripetano in futuro

CD0307 — Incident investigation, Investi.question: Qual é a finalidade de investigar incidentes e usar o conhecimento obtido com a investigação? Selecione A melhor resposta.
options: Uma redução ou até eliminação desses incidentes no futuro
